scope: Carrier-conditioned MiniMax-H3 test-time scaling and contact-causality audit for ordered T-shirt folding
summary: A predeclared four-candidate carrier-conditioned MiniMax-H3 run completed with two 32-step and two 40-step seeds. All four candidates were rejected. The best 40-step output satisfied the original camera-frame order, continuity, body-fold, bundle-move, first-frame, background, and compact-terminal checks, but both sleeve-length gates failed. Native-resolution review also found stationary manipulators while the shirt folded itself. A new frozen gripper-proximity gate replayed all four candidates and rejected contact_precedes_cloth_motion for every one. No video is accepted or delivered.
evidence: Candidate 3 maximum sleeve-length relative deviations were 0.231 viewer-left and 0.160 viewer-right against the unchanged 0.08 limit
All four contact-audit evidence files report contact_precedes_cloth_motion=false
lessons: A continuous cloth carrier improved task order but caused H3 to copy self-moving cloth when manipulator motion was absent from the carrier.
Increasing inference steps from 32 to 40 improved downstream action ordering but did not repair either sleeve-length invariant.
A physical-video harness must freeze and track manipulator points as well as cloth material points; language-only contact instructions are not acceptance evidence.
The analytic carrier transform must use the same camera-pixel rotation convention as OpenCV rendering even when both transforms independently preserve segment length.
limitations: The gripper proximity gate is 2-D visual causal evidence and does not establish force, grasp stability, collision safety, joint feasibility, or real-robot success.
The attempted whole-arm translated carrier produced holes and disconnected limbs in visual preflight and was rejected before GPU generation.
No current MiniMax-H3 candidate passes the immutable sleeve-length and contact-causality gates.
next_actions: Use a temporally coherent articulated robot or simulator-derived contact carrier with connected arm geometry rather than translating raster arm regions.
Predeclare the contact-aware tracking contract before the next candidate generation and keep the existing sleeve limits unchanged.
